Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 General 2 Yahtzee 3 Yam 4 Yacht 5 Yatzy 6 Maxy Yatzy 7 Crag 8 Random 9 Simultaneous Mode 10 Triple Mode 11 Examples General A player rolls the dice to begin a turn. They are then allowed to reroll dice, with each reroll being any number of those dice. (In BGA, you click on the dice that you want to reroll.) After those rerolls, or when the player chooses to stop rolling, the player must choose which category to score the final result. There are limited scoring categories, and each must be used for one of the rounds. This can often force a player to take a zero score for some categories. Yahtzee - Roll 5 dice with 2 rerolls per turn - Get 63 points in the upper section to get 35 bonus points - Three of a kind scores the sum of all dice - Four of a kind scores the sum of all dice - Full house scores 25 points - Small straight scores 30 points - Large straight scores 40 points - Five of a kind scores 50 points. Each extra five of a kind scores 100 bonus points and must also be scored in another category -- A five of a kind can be used to score a full house, small straight, or large straight when the five of a kind box and the corresponding upper section box have been filled already - Chance scores the sum of all dice Yam - Roll 5 dice with 2 rerolls per turn - Get 60 points in the upper section to get the difference between the upper section score and 30 points - Plus section and minus section can be filled by any combination. Score the difference between plus and minus, or 0 if minus is higher than plus - Four of a kind scores 40 points plus the sum of all dice - Full house scores 30 points plus the sum of all dice - Small straight scores 45 points - Large straight scores 50 points - Five of a kind scores 50 points plus the sum of all dice - Rigole (four dice of the same number and a die of the opposite number) scores 50 points Yacht - Roll 5 dice with 2 rerolls per turn - No upper section bonus - Four of a kind scores the sum of four of a kind - Full house scores the sum of all dice - Low straight (1-2-3-4-5) scores 30 points - High straight (2-3-4-5-6) scores 30 points - Five of a kind scores 50 points - Chance scores the sum of all dice Yatzy - Roll 5 dice with 2 rerolls per turn - Get 63 points in the upper section to get 50 bonus points - One pair scores the sum of one pair - Two pairs scores the sum of two pairs - Three of a kind scores the sum of three of a kind - Four of a kind scores the sum of four of a kind - Full house scores the sum of all dice - Low straight (1-2-3-4-5) scores 15 points - High straight (2-3-4-5-6) scores 20 points - Five of a kind scores 50 points - Chance scores the sum of all dice Maxy Yatzy - Roll 6 dice - Gain 2 rerolls per turn -- Unused rerolls are saved and can be used later - Get 84 points in the upper section to get 100 bonus points - One pair scores the sum of the dice in the pair - Two pairs score the sum of the dice in the pairs - Three pairs score the sum of all dice - Three of a kind scores the sum of the dice in the three of a kind - Four of a kind scores the sum of the dice in the four of a kind - Five of a kind scores the sum of the dice in the five of a kind - Low straight (1-2-3-4-5) scores 15 points - High straight (2-3-4-5-6) scores 20 points - Full straight (1-2-3-4-5-6) scores 21 points - Full house scores the sum of the dice in the full house - Castle (three dice of one number and three dice of another number) scores the sum of all dice - Tower (four dice of one number and two dice of another number) scores the sum of all dice - Six of a kind scores 100 points - Chance scores the sum of all dice Crag - Rolls

[Rating: 1/10] Six hours.  That's how long it took my family and I to play one game of this.  It is also the only time we ever played it.  Six hours.  I'll never get that time back you know.

[Rating: 1/10] I've had more fun with office filing.. and I'd rather watch a mosquito suck my blood than watch a bunch of d6 rolling meaninglessly across the table.  [i]Update July 2006[/i] - It was pointed out to me that this is a good game to teach counting to kids. However, I can say the same for Blackjack so Yawn-tzee still looses out.

[Rating: 1/10] This game gave all other dice games a bad name that stuck for almost a century!  Why not just roll the dice ONCE and call a winner????

[Rating: 1/10] My in-laws love this game.  It's a solitary game where you compare your totals at the end.  You just might as well play at home and call each other to see who won.

[Rating: 1/10] Technically I own enough dice to play this and know how to play, but I find it slightly more entertaining than watching paint dry.

[Rating: 1/10] I would rather have hot pokers shoved down my pants than hear "yathzee!" one more time.

[Rating: 1/10] I have never ever enjoyed this game.  I just detest it.  Never will I ever play.  CHILDHOOD GAME ???

[Rating: 1/10] I know Yahtzee is a popular game, I just think it's boring. You roll dice, mark a score. Roll dice, mark a score.
